The Northwest is one of the two sub-regions which make up the Northern Midland and Mountainous Regions of Northern Vietnam. Geography[edit] Further information on the mountain range: Sông Mã Range History[edit] A large area of the region was previously a part of the Sip Song Chau Tai, Tai-Meo Autonomous Region, which was dissolved in 1954. It was renamed the "Northwest Autonomous Region" (Khu Tự trị Tây Bắc) in 1961, in order to not highlight just two of the many ethnic groups in this zone. pagesRead.content: From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Locations of cities in Vietnam: (listed from top to bottom) • Hà Nội • Quảng Ninh • Hải Phòng • Huế • Đà Nẵng • Đồng Nai • Hồ Chí Minh City • Cần ThơSkylines of Vietnamese cities In Vietnam, cities (Vietnamese: thành phố) are a type of administrative division. Since the 2025 reforms to local government, cities only exist as first-level administrative divisions, equivalent to a province and fully designated as the centrally-governed cities (Vietnamese: thành phố trực thuộc trung ương, lit. 'city directly subordinate to the centre (central government)'). City status requires a resolution of the National Assembly of Vietnam. As with provinces, they are divided into urban wards, rural communes, and, where appropriate, island special zones. Prior to 2025, cities also existed at the district level, and may be subject to the administration of a province or of a centrally-governed city. Prior to 2025 reforms[edit] Prior to the amendment of the Constitution on June 16, 2025, Vietnamese cities were divided into 2 main administrative types: centrally-governed cities (thành phố trực thuộc trung ương) and provincial cities (thành phố trực thuộc tỉnh). Municipal cities were considered district-level administrative units within the municipalities.[1] Cities were further assessed and categorized under the urban area classification resolution, which includes six classes: Special (Vietnamese: Loại đặc biệt), Class I, Class II, Class III, Class IV and Class V. Municipalities and Municipal Cities were given Class I (With the exception of Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City being Special Class). Provincial Cities were assigned Class I, Class II, Class III depending on classification criteria.[2] After 2025 reforms[edit] Main article: Administrative reform in Vietnam 2025 After the amendment of the Constitution, centrally-governed cities became the only administrative units defined as 'cities.' [3][4] The amendment resulted in the dissolution of provincial cities, which rendered the urban area classification resolution outdated.
